doc.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002

title: Bird's insecurity, drinking and the pressure of being a pioneer
summary: She gives her personal view of Bird's sadness and fear late in life and the chemical substitutes people use.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: How did he feel about being – as you said — a God? Was he confident about his own abilities?

I think in the end, when he was drinking so much after he had put down the heroin and he got into really, really heavy drinking, people drink and drug because of low self esteem and an insecurity and a fear. And I can say this because I’ve been there, you know, and I have since like been getting myself together for the last twenty-some years. But unfortunately Bird did not find that way. I feel that he was — I don’t know, I got the feeling from Bird that he knew that he had originated a new music, a new way to play, to hear, whatever you want to call it, whatever it is. He knew that he was a pioneer of this bebop, one of the pioneers of this bebop music. I think what happened with Bird towards the end was he was afraid that he was not able to go on and keep progressing. Sometimes we have to be settled into where we are. Okay, this is what I did, this is how I do it, I found my peak. That doesn’t mean I can’t spurt off in other little places, but am I going to go another step? Am I going to go like a pyramid? Am I going to keep building? And you can sometimes get stuck there. And I know that. Of course Bird to me was a genius. And again it’s that transient thing with me, that he wasn’t supposed to go any further. But I think that he, in the end, he was very sad. And I think, I got the feeling that there was a

part of him that he wanted to be like I’m the Bird you know, and there was another part of him that didn’t want all that pressure of being this pioneer, and do I have to keep doing this? When can I relax and just enjoy life? And that never seemed to happen. This is my own personal feeling about Bird and the time that I spent with him and got to know him. And I could be dead wrong. But this is the feeling that I got from him is that I don’t want to be up here, I want to play my music the way I play it, and I want to enjoy my life. And sometimes when you’re insecure like that with having that feeling of I’d better keep — you have to take substitutes or whatever you want to call them, what do we call them, I can’t remember anything anymore.

Yes. Chemical help. Yes. Chemical substitutes to sort of like not bring ourselves down or kind of feel a little better or more secure, to get rid of the fear. It’s a fear. That’s what it is, it’s the fear of like oh my God, how long before they catch up with me, and then where do I go. Do you know what I mean? Now, you know, when you’ve really settled into what you do and have your own thing, who cares? Please catch up with me. I hope you do.
